title: Retention policy matrix and automated evidence for prompts, outputs, and telemetry
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Goal:
Define a practical, auditable retention policy matrix for: prompt inputs, model responses, request logs (headers/metadata), and operational metrics. Deliver console and API controls to configure retention per-organization and per-route, with automated evidence/report bundles for compliance teams and auditors.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Retention tier definitions and suggested defaults for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Console UI and API design for configuring retention windows (per-tenant and per-route) and override rules.
- Automated evidence/reporting automation: periodic export of retention settings, deletion proofs, and retention-change audit trail.
- Acceptance criteria and rollout plan for enabling legal-hold and emergency forensics without breaking SLOs.

Out of scope (to be tracked separately):
- Underlying low-level backup/replication changes in third-party infra (handled by ENG-2910).
- Long-term cold-archive storage pricing model (follow-up).

Proposed retention matrix (recommended default tiers):
- Ephemeral: 0-7 days — for raw prompts/responses used in low-sensitivity workloads; default for trial orgs.
- Short-term: 30 days — common default for Hosted API, balances debugging and privacy.
- Standard: 90 days — recommended for most customers that need incident debugging and ML telemetry.
- Long-term: 365 days — for customers with compliance requirements or extended analysis needs.
- Indefinite: customer opt-in with explicit legal/contract approval.

Proposed per-data-type defaults and policy notes:
- Prompts (input text): default = Short-term 30d. Consider opt-out/opt-in depending on model access levels; PII redaction recommended before storage.
- Responses (generated outputs): default = Short-term 30d. Mark outputs tied to customer-owned knowledge bases as eligible for longer retention only by contract.
- Request logs (headers, IPs, API keys masked): default = Short-term 30d. Sensitive fields (authorization tokens) must never be persisted in plaintext.
- Metrics and aggregated telemetry: default = Standard 90d for time-series; raw debug traces kept Ephemeral 7d unless flagged.
- KV-cache and model-internal cached artifacts: retention aligned with model session lifetime; not stored as persistent PII.

Evidence and reporting automation features:
- Retention configuration snapshot exports (JSON/CSV) on demand and monthly scheduled exports per org.
- Deletion-proof artifacts: when retention TTL expires, generate a signed deletion event with timestamp, deleted objects counts, and checksum of deleted blob IDs; store proof in audit log for configurable retention.
- Legal-hold mode: suspend automated deletions for specified orgs/keys and surface a legal-hold indicator in Console and API.
- Compliance report generator: single-click package that includes current retention settings, audit trail of changes, deletion-proofs, and per-route request counts for the period.
- Evidence delivery: secure S3/GCS export or ephemeral signed URL to compliance contact; optional envelope encryption with customer KMS for Private deployments.

UI/API design highlights:
- Console: per-organization settings, per-route overrides, visual retention timeline, legal-hold toggle, and "Generate Compliance Bundle" button.
- API: SetRetentionPolicy(org_id, route_id, data_type, ttl_days, reason, effective_from); GetRetentionPolicy(...); GenerateComplianceBundle(org_id, range_start, range_end).
- Defaults: enforce safe defaults (Short-term 30d) for new orgs; require admin approval for Indefinite retention.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Deletion strategy: soft-delete + background hard-deletion pipeline to allow for safe rollbacks during rollout. Proofs generated after hard deletion.
- Backups & snapshots: ensure deletion requests cascade or are tracked for downstream backups; need coordination with ENG-2910 (backup retention) to avoid orphaned copies.
- Cost vs retention: longer retention increases storage and egress costs; provide conservative defaults and price guidance in Console.
- Incident debugging: too-aggressive retention hampers root-cause analysis; consider short-term extended retention for flagged incidents with auto-sunset.
- Private deployments: support customer-controlled KMS and storage endpoints; retention enforcement may differ per-customer contract.

Acceptance criteria (must be true for ticket to be Done):
- Product spec and retention matrix approved by Security and Legal.
- Console settings implemented (per-org and per-route) with unit tests for UI validation.
- API endpoints implemented and documented in the developer docs.
- Automated compliance bundle generation producing signed deletion proofs and manifest for a sample org.
- E2E test that verifies legal-hold suspends deletions and that removal of legal-hold resumes deletion.
- Security review completed and SEC sign-off logged (SEC-102).

Rollout plan:
1) Phase 1 (Feature flag ON for internal orgs): implement API + backend retention TTL and proof generator; enable for internal test orgs.
2) Phase 2 (Beta customers): enable Console UI and scheduled compliance bundle exports for opt-in customers.
3) Phase 3 (GA): default policies for new orgs, migrations for existing orgs with communication plan and self-serve controls.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Should prompts with PII be automatically redacted before storage or simply surfaced as a policy and left to customers? (Legal prefers automatic redaction for Hosted.)
- Deletion proof format — signed JSON manifest vs append-only ledger entry. Ledger would be stronger but higher engineering cost.
- Retention of metrics stored in third-party systems (Prometheus/CloudWatch) — do we provide a sync/confirmation of deletion?

- Kick off spike with ENG to validate deletion-proof implementation and backup interactions (ENG-2873).
- Prepare communication plan and beta customer list for Phase 2.
